investigations.title: Unprotected left-turn regression after v4.3.0
investigations.summary: INC-0412 was not a one-off. At the two occluded unprotected-left sites in Ridgeview, planner-uncertainty flags went from 1.8 per operating day on v4.2.0 to 14.2 on v4.3.0, and safety-critical takeovers from 2 in 24 days to 7 in 14 days. The rise is concentrated at dusk and at the most occluded site. v4.3.1 cut flags to 6.3 per day and saw 2 safety-critical takeovers in 10 days, but flags are still above the v4.2.0 baseline, so the action stays open.

timeline.event: Box trucks noted parking at Marlow loading zone after 3 pm, blocking view of oncoming lane.
v4.3.0 rolled out fleet-wide. Sim gate passed; no occluded-left low-light scenarios in suite.
Planner-uncertainty and hard-brake flags at Marlow and Hale rise above the W1-W4 baseline band (leading indicator).
VSO-17 reports AV 'pauses then commits late' at Marlow around sunset.
Similar takeover at Hale Rd & Pine St.
occlusion_high flag at Marlow Ave & 5th St (AV-06, dusk, sunset 18:03).
planner_uncertainty flag while AV creeps into the turn.
VSO-15 takes over and brakes; TTC 1.1 s. Oncoming car emerged from behind parked box truck.
hard_brake recorded. Min separation 2.3 m, no contact (INC-0412, S0).
Investigation opened; site pattern escalated to planning team with rate evidence.
v4.3.1 hotfix restores conservative creep when the oncoming lane is occluded.

evidence.item: Intervention log, filtered to Marlow and Hale
evidence.finding: Safety-critical takeovers: v4.2.0 2 (24 days), v4.3.0 7 (14 days), v4.3.1 2 (10 days).

evidence.item: Model flags at the same sites
evidence.finding: planner_uncertainty per operating day: v4.2.0 1.8, v4.3.0 14.2, v4.3.1 6.3. Rose the week before INC-0412.
Dusk km per week roughly doubled across the period as sunsets moved earlier, so rates are compared per dusk km, not raw counts.
Effect scales with occlusion: Marlow (high) > Hale > Market St (medium) > Harbor Blvd (low, no clear change).
v4.3.0 suite had no occluded oncoming-lane scenarios in low light.
Operators described the behaviour 6 days before the near miss; reports were not linked to the release.

whys: Why did the near miss happen? The AV committed to the turn while an oncoming car was hidden behind a parked truck.
Why did it commit? v4.3.0's new yielding cost terms shortened the creep-and-look phase when the oncoming lane was occluded.
Why wasn't this caught before release? The sim regression suite had no occluded unprotected-left scenarios in low light.
Why did it reach an incident after rollout? Rising flags and operator reports were not monitored per site after the release.
Why not? There was no post-release watch list tying leading indicators to the change that shipped.

Software / model: v4.3.0 planner cost change reduced creep behaviour under occlusion
Uncertainty flag raised but did not trigger a more conservative policy
Process / controls: No post-release leading-indicator watch for 2 weeks
Environment: Parked box trucks block sightline after 3 pm
Earlier sunsets moved PM shifts into dusk
People: VSO-15 responded correctly (0.7 s); operator reports existed but were not escalated
Data: Field observations stored as free text, not linked to software version

investigations.root_cause: A planner change in v4.3.0 reduced creep-and-look behaviour on unprotected left turns with an occluded oncoming lane, and the release gate had no low-light occluded scenarios to catch it.

actions.action: Add 64 occluded-left low-light scenarios to release gate
Restrict PM unprotected lefts at Marlow when loading zone occupied (route avoid) until rate returns to baseline
Two-week post-release watch list for every release: site-level flag and takeover rates vs baseline
Tag field observations with vehicle, site and software version

limitations: Counts at two sites are small; rates per version have wide uncertainty.
Dusk exposure changes with season, which partly confounds the before/after comparison.
Occlusion level per pass is inferred from flags, not measured directly.

investigations.title: Late takeover by fatigued VSO on extended shift
investigations.summary: VSO-24 worked 19 of 40 shifts longer than the 4.0 h limit from week 5; the fleet had 31 over-limit shifts in total. INC-0419 happened 6.1 h into a 6.3 h shift, at night in rain. DMS flagged drowsiness 6 minutes earlier and ops acknowledged it after 9 min 10 s. Takeover reaction was 2.4 s against a fleet median under 1 s.

timeline.event: VSO-24 begins covering extended PM blocks (5.5-6.5 h) on AV-10/AV-11.
Ride-along auditor notes VSO-24 yawning in hour 5; says they cover extra PM blocks most days.
VSO-24 starts 6.3 h shift on AV-10 (Old Town). Rain from late afternoon.
Eyes off road 2.6 s.
Drowsiness alert (7.8 s). Ops acknowledgement at 20:44:20, 9 min 10 s later.
Eyes off road 3.1 s.
perception_low_conf on curb edge, Rowan St (street lighting out, wet).
Lateral-deviation alert as AV moves right for oncoming van.
VSO-24 takeover, reaction 2.4 s. Right front wheel strikes curb at 14 km/h (INC-0419, S1).
Investigation opened; VSO-24 stood down from PM shifts pending review.

evidence.finding: 19 VSO-24 shifts over 4.0 h; scheduling tool did not block them.

evidence.item: DMS events by hour into shift
evidence.finding: Fleet drowsiness rate rises sharply after hour 4; VSO-24's rate is the highest in the fleet.
Fleet median under 1 s; VSO-24 reactions lengthen after hour 5.
Share of alerts acknowledged after 5 min is highest after 18:00, when ops staffing is thinner.
Fatigue observed 6 days earlier; Rowan St lighting outage reported 4 days later confirms dark conditions.

whys: Why did the wheel hit the curb? The VSO took over 2.4 s after the alert, too late to correct.
Why was the takeover slow? The VSO was drowsy, 6.1 h into a shift, at night.
Why was the VSO on a 6.3 h shift? The scheduling tool allowed blocks over the 4.0 h policy and this VSO covered them repeatedly.
Why did the drowsiness alert not stop the shift? The alert waited 9 min for acknowledgement and there is no rule to stand a VSO down after a drowsiness alert.
Why? The fatigue controls are written policy but not enforced in tools or monitored in reporting.

People: Fatigue from extended and repeated PM shifts
Eyes-off-road events in the minutes before the event
Process / controls: 4.0 h shift limit not enforced by scheduling tool
No stand-down rule after DMS drowsiness alert
Environment: Night, rain, street lighting out on Rowan St
Narrow two-way road with oncoming van
Software / model: Low perception confidence on curb edge in dark, wet conditions
Data: Fatigue indicators existed in DMS data but were not trended per VSO

investigations.root_cause: Fatigue controls were not enforced: the scheduling tool allowed shifts beyond the 4.0 h limit, and a DMS drowsiness alert did not lead to a timely response or stand-down.

actions.action: Hard-block shifts over 4.0 h in the scheduling tool
Mandatory stand-down and ops call after any DMS drowsiness alert
Add evening ops staffing to meet 5-min DMS acknowledgement SLA
Weekly per-VSO fatigue indicator in the safety pack (DMS rate after hour 4, overtime shifts)
Report Rowan St lighting outage to city; night route restriction until fixed

limitations: DMS measures eye and head behaviour; it does not measure fatigue directly.
One VSO's data cannot separate individual factors from shift pattern; both are addressed.

investigations.title: AV-09 lane bias after windshield replacement
investigations.summary: AV-09 returned to service on Oct 9 after an external windshield replacement without a camera recalibration. Over the next 11 days it logged 29 localization-drift flags (vs 1 in the 11 days after recalibration) and two operator reports of left lane bias before the Oct 15 encroachment.

timeline.event: Windshield replaced by vendor; calibration check 'not performed'; returned to service same day.
AV-09 localization_drift and perception_low_conf flags rise to several times the fleet rate.
VSO-22: AV-09 tracks left of lane centre on curves.
Second report; logged in shift notes, not escalated.
Repeated localization_drift on Old Bridge Rd.
VSO-22 steers right after ~0.35 m centre-line crossing (INC-0398, S0).
Vehicle anomaly matched to maintenance record; recalibration booked for first vendor slot (Oct 20). AV-09 stayed in service meanwhile.
Front camera extrinsic recalibration; flags return to fleet level.

evidence.finding: AV-09 was the top weekly anomaly in W3-W4 for localization drift.
Calibration 'not performed' after windshield work on Oct 9.
29 drift flags in 11 days before vs 1 after.
Operators noticed the bias 2 days before the event.

whys: Why did AV-09 cross the centre line? Lane position was biased left on curves.
Why? Front camera extrinsics were off after the windshield was replaced.
Why was it not recalibrated? The return-to-service checklist did not require calibration after glass work by a vendor.
Why wasn't the bias caught sooner? Operator reports stayed in shift notes and vehicle-level flag trends were not reviewed daily.
Why? No owner for per-vehicle anomaly review.

Vehicle / hardware: Camera extrinsic calibration invalid after windshield replacement
Process / controls: Return-to-service checklist gap for vendor glass work
No rule to stand a vehicle down while a calibration defect is open
Data: Per-vehicle anomaly signal present from day 1 but not reviewed

investigations.root_cause: The return-to-service process did not require camera recalibration after a vendor windshield replacement.

actions.action: Add mandatory calibration check after any glass, sensor-mount or bumper work
Daily per-vehicle anomaly review (flag z-score vs fleet)
Stand vehicles down until any open sensor-calibration defect is closed

limitations: Magnitude of the calibration error was not measured before correction.

investigations.title: Construction zone at Dock St & Pier 3
investigations.summary: Precautionary takeovers at Dock St & Pier 3 rose from the week the lane closure started (Oct 26). The rise is environmental: it appears on every software version, is limited to one site, and matches field reports. INC-0427 was a 6 km/h contact with a wind-displaced cone.

timeline.event: Lane closure with cones begins at Dock St & Pier 3 (4 weeks).
Precautionary takeovers and ood_scene flags rise at the site only.
Cones drift into the open lane in wind.
ood_scene, then perception_low_conf at the closure (AV-02).
VSO-04 takeover 1.0 s; cone contacted at 6 km/h (INC-0427, S1, property only).
Contractor ballasts cones; closure extended.

evidence.finding: Increase begins W6 at this site only; other Harbor sites flat.
Most takeovers at the site are attributed 'external', not to a stack module.
Confirm closure start, cone drift, and fix.

whys: Why the contact? A cone displaced by wind sat inside the travel lane.
Why did the AV not avoid it fully? It was classified as low-priority static debris in an unusual (out-of-distribution) scene.
Why was the AV routed through? Temporary closures are not fed into routing or ODD restrictions.

Environment: Temporary lane closure, unballasted cones drifting in wind
Software / model: Out-of-distribution scene; displaced cone treated as low-priority object
Process / controls: No process to restrict ODD around reported temporary works

investigations.root_cause: Temporary works reported by operators were not used to restrict routing, exposing the fleet to an unusual scene with drifting cones.

actions.action: Route around Dock St closure until removed
Process: field-reported temporary works trigger an ODD review within 24 h
Add drifting-cone scenarios to perception eval set

limitations: Pre-closure baseline at this site is short (5 weeks).

investigations.title: Rear-end collision by third party
investigations.summary: The AV was stationary at a red light for 6.2 s with brake lights on when a third-party car struck it at ~12 km/h. Data shows no AV contribution and an attentive VSO.

timeline.event: AV-07 stops at red light, College Ave; brake lights on.
Rear impact ~12 km/h from third-party car. No injuries.
Police and insurer notified; dashcam and logs preserved.

evidence.finding: Stationary 6.2 s before impact; no harsh braking.
No DMS events in the 10 minutes before impact.

whys: Why the collision? Following driver did not stop. No AV behaviour contributed.

Environment: Morning traffic, third-party following too closely

investigations.root_cause: Third-party driver error. No AV or VSO contribution found.

actions.action: Rear bumper repair and rear radar recalibration
